benefits: Real XML attribute support: JSON keys starting with @ become XML attributes and back again.
Nested JSON objects become nested XML elements, and repeated elements become arrays.
Dot-notation flattening turns nested JSON into clean CSV columns like address.city.
One page for JSON, XML and CSV in any direction, with one-click swap.

faqs.a: Prefix the key with @. {"user": {"@id": "1", "name": "Aarav"}} becomes <user id="1"><name>Aarav</name></user>. Going the other way, XML attributes become @-prefixed keys in the JSON.
faqs.q: How do I make an XML attribute from JSON?

faqs.a: Use the #text key. {"note": {"@lang": "en", "#text": "Hello"}} becomes <note lang="en">Hello</note>. Mixed content is preserved on the way back too.
faqs.q: How do I put text inside an element that has attributes?

faqs.a: Yes. Repeated child elements with the same tag become a JSON array: <tags><tag>a</tag><tag>b</tag></tags> becomes {"tags": {"tag": ["a", "b"]}}.
Turn on Flatten nested objects. {"address": {"city": "Mumbai"}} becomes the CSV column address.city. With it off, nested values are written as compact JSON text in the cell.
faqs.q: How does nested JSON become CSV?

faqs.a: CSV has no notion of attributes or nesting, so XML attributes become @-prefixed columns and nested elements become either flattened columns or JSON text, depending on the flatten toggle.
faqs.q: What happens to XML attributes in CSV output?

limitations: CSV output cannot preserve the distinction between attributes and elements beyond the @ prefix.
Flattening uses dot notation, which can collide with keys that already contain dots.
XML namespaces are simplified to local names.
Very large inputs (tens of MB) can make the browser tab sluggish.

json-xml-csv-converter.workedExample:
XML to JSON input:
<users>
  <user id="1">
    <name>Aarav Sharma</name>
  </user>
</users>

JSON output:
[
  {
    "@id": "1",
    "name": "Aarav Sharma"
  }
]

The id attribute becomes the @id key.

JSON to CSV input (flatten on):
[{"name":"Aarav","address":{"city":"Mumbai"}}]

CSV output:
name,address.city
Aarav,Mumbai

1 record, 2 flattened columns.
